Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye

Record Class EyePlacement

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.EyePlacement
public record EyePlacement(net.minecraft.world.phys.Vec3 position, float eyeScale, float irisScale, float depth, float inclination, float azimuth, int crossTarget) extends Record
The placement (geometry) of a single eye on a mob: offset from the attach joint, sizes, and aim. Config-only — never carried on an eye item (that's appearance, see AppearanceOverride).

Aim is two angles, not a quaternion: inclination from the part's +Y axis and azimuth from its +X axis (degrees). The eye's pupil faces local -Z by default; roll is irrelevant (the eye is rotationally symmetric about its look axis), so two angles suffice.

depth multiplies the eye's thickness along its look axis (1.0 = the standard proportions). The eye's back face sits at its attach position and the body extends forward, so a deeper eye protrudes further from the model — enough to envelop a modeled eyeball that sticks out of the head (e.g. the Ice and Fire cyclops). Cornea and iris stretch together, so the iris always stays in front of the cornea.

crossTarget is the index of another eye in the same head that this eye rolls its pupil toward during the cross-eye behavior (see EyeBehavior#CROSS_EYE); NO_CROSS_TARGET means this eye doesn't cross. It's a within-head index into that head's eyes list.

Everything is float: these are authored through /sg commands whose args parse as float, and the renderer consumes them as float. Holding them as double would only widen 0.22 into 0.2199999988079071 on its way back out to the (human-edited) datapack. position keeps Vec3 for the vector arithmetic, but serializes at float precision for the same reason.

    • MAP_CODEC

      public static final com.mojang.serialization.MapCodec<EyePlacement> MAP_CODEC
      MapCodec (flat fields) so EyeDefinition can sit placement beside appearance.

      Every field is required. A config has exactly one shape on disk, so absent-vs-default is a distinction nothing reads — and making the fields optional would mean encode silently elides any value equal to its default, leaving files whose meaning drifts with the code.
